title: PHP2Shell Detection
content_md: PHP2Shell detection matters because the window between a patch and real-world exploitation can be a single day. PHP2Shell is the name for two unauthenticated remote code execution flaws in PHP core, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, both rated CVSS v4.0 9.2. No authentication is needed, so any exposed PHP application on an unpatched release is a target. In the sample below, exploitation surfaces as a PHP worker crash followed by commands running as the web server user. This article covers PHP2Shell detection using a log sample analyzed in LogTotal, a log analysis tool that matches events to known threats. Below, we explain the vulnerability context, where the logs came from, what LogTotal found, and how to respond. PHP2Shell Analysis Both PHP2Shell flaws score 9.2 under CVSS v4.0, and both can be reached without authentication on any PHP installation that serves web requests. To read the log sample correctly, it helps to know how each bug works, how fast the disclosure unfolded, and which installations are exposed. Get Started For Free Vulnerability details for PHP2Shell The two CVEs are separate memory-safety bugs in how PHP handles a request. Either one lets an attacker run code as the web server user. CVE-2026-109618, out-of-memory corruption. When PHP runs out of memory partway through setting up a request, internal data is left half built, and the cleanup code then trusts it.
